Lessons.Title: Mondrian's Art (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs: Optional 2021 Grade4 U01 L08 original source Student Task Statements three-page PDF. Goal: apply previously learned area, factors, prime and composite number classification to an original creative artwork; no new numbered standard.
Warm-up Notice and Wonder (10 minutes): two teacher-supplied attributed public-domain Piet Mondrian paintings; identify rectangles and discuss equal/different areas; open teacher-reviewed discussion.

Activity1 My Mondrian Outline (20 minutes): draw the ENTIRE 18-by-24 grid partitioned into at least 12 rectangles. Include two DIFFERENT rectangles of equal area and one prime-area region. Try either challenge: all but two rectangle areas prime, or no pair of rectangles sharing an entire side. Teacher examines the entire partition and labels; there is no automatic drawing grader.

Activity2 Analyze the Rectangles (20 minutes): exchange work, identify same-area rectangles, rectangles with prime area, rectangles with composite area and which extension was completed. Use dimension measurements and factor pairs; color and gallery-display artwork, with mathematical sticky-note questions.

Independent Edulytics formative reflection, not publisher original: 3×4 and2×6 both have area12; 1×7 area7 is prime. Explain these facts and your own design choice. Teacher reviews reasoning, numeric supplementary questions are not full task grading.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rectangle area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Unit squares in a rectangular region.

KeyConcepts.Title: Prime region area
KeyConcepts.Definition: Area >1 whose only positive divisors are1 and itself.

KeyConcepts.Title: Whole-artwork constraints
KeyConcepts.Definition: Properties checked over the full grid.
KeyConcepts.Rule: ≥12 regions; different equal-area pair; prime-area region; chosen extension.
